Question B-006-012-005.

Why the correct answer is right: A horizontal half-wave dipole radiates broadside to the wire. If its ends point north and south, the broadside directions are east and west.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Radiates mostly to the South and North": South and north are the directions off the wire ends, where a half-wave dipole has nulls rather than maximum radiation.
- sourceIndex 2: "Radiates mostly to the South": A simple dipole pattern is not one-ended toward only south; off the south end is a null direction in this orientation.
- sourceIndex 3: "Radiates equally in all directions": A horizontal half-wave dipole is not omnidirectional in free space. It has broadside maxima and end nulls.
